'Which is more: 23 mL or 56 mL?' offers 56, 55, 58 and 57, so the losing quantity is absent and the only option drawn from the stem is the key; the 12 L against 15 L item and the 69 mL against 55 mL item behave the same way. A pupil scoring full marks may never have compared the two capacities at all.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The competency speaks of two containers, yet no container is ever described, only bare numbers with a unit. Every item is phrased as which is more, so the equal-capacity case and the which-holds-less direction are both absent from the fourteen samples.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Both quantities in each pair share a unit, so no conversion between litres and millilitres is required, and comparing whole numbers of up to four digits is within the Grade 3 Quarter 2 number range.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: One sentence pattern accounts for the entire node. Nothing presents two vessels to be judged by sight, nothing asks for the difference between the two capacities, and nothing frames the comparison as a situation such as choosing which container to fill.

competency_alignment.rationale: Many pairs are so lopsided, 1 L against 22 L and 8 L against 447 L among them, that no real comparison judgement is involved, while the genuinely close pair of 12 L and 15 L is rare. Difficulty is being set by the size of the gap and the digit count rather than by the comparison itself.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: A container of 447 L, and a 3348 mL reading against a 12 mL one, sit well outside the vessels a Grade 3 pupil handles, and the surrounding options such as 3347, 3349 and 3350 turn the item into digit matching.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The two-direction aspect is well handled, but the multi-step qualifier the competency states is met by only one item, the figure that slides 2 spaces left, then 1 more space left, then 4 spaces up. Every other slide is a single move in each of two directions. The drawing verb is likewise served only indirectly, by predicting where a shape would land.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Direction pairs are covered reasonably, left with down, right with up, and right with down, and the inverse case appears where a point moving from one position to another must be described as a slide. But composing several steps before reporting the net effect, which is the distinguishing feature of this competency, occurs once in nine samples.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Four items work in ordered-pair coordinate notation, asking where a circle at grid coordinate (2, 4) lands and giving the key (7, 3). Formal coordinate pairs with independent arithmetic on each component are heavier than the informal grid-and-spaces language that the rest of the node uses and that suits Grade 3.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: All items are mcq, and two stems each appear twice with only reordered options, the 5-left-and-2-down naming item and the circle at (2, 4) item, so four of the nine rendered samples are duplicate pairs. The invariance item about whether the orientation or shape changes is the one genuinely distinct framing.

competency_alignment.rationale: The items do build the same idea from different sides, naming the movement, counting its directions, composing steps, predicting the landing point, recovering the slide from before-and-after positions, and recognising that a translation preserves shape. All of these are translation reasoning rather than a substituted axis.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Slide distances are at most 5 spaces and grid positions stay in single digits, so the arithmetic never distracts from the geometric idea, which is the right emphasis for a Quarter 4 transformation competency.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The competency is about identifying symmetric shapes by drawing the line of symmetry, yet most items ask for a count of lines instead. Only two items concern where the line actually runs, the one asking in which direction the letter B's line of symmetry runs and the heart item asking whether both sides match when a vertical line is drawn down the centre.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The sample set spans figures with one, two, three, four and unlimited lines, using an isosceles triangle, the letter H, an equilateral triangle, a square and a circle, so the range of symmetry counts is genuinely exercised rather than defaulting to the single-line case.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Classifying triangles by side length, with stems naming an isosceles triangle and an equilateral triangle, presumes triangle-type vocabulary heavier than a Quarter 4 symmetry lesson needs, and the circle key 'Infinite (unlimited)' introduces unboundedness which Grade 3 has no formal handle on, though the gloss helps.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: All samples are mcq and none presents a set of figures from which the symmetric one must be picked, which is the identification act the competency describes. The letter B stem is also emitted twice with only the options reshuffled.

competency_alignment.rationale: Each item stays on line symmetry itself rather than sliding into rotation or tessellation, and the definition item establishing that a line of symmetry gives equal halves that are mirror images underpins every counting item in the node.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: This competency sets no numeric ceiling, and the only numbers involved are symmetry counts from 0 to 4 plus the unlimited case, which is the correct and complete set of magnitudes for the figures used.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The competency asks for a figure to be completed, but almost every item completes a single point rather than a figure, for instance placing the mirror image of a point 3 grid units to the left of a vertical line. Only the butterfly item, where 3 dots on the left wing must be matched on the right, works at the level of a figure.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Vertical and horizontal lines of symmetry are both used, and reflection is asked in both directions, left to right at several seeds and right to left at seed 601, so the generator does not assume a single fixed axis or a single side.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Grid-unit distances stay between 2 and 5 and the reasoning is one equal-distance step, which fits Grade 3 Quarter 4. Describing positions as so many grid units above or to the left of the line avoids coordinate notation, which is appropriate restraint at this grade.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Beyond the two principle statements and the butterfly, the node is one reflection item repeated, and two stems recur verbatim across seeds, the 3-units-left point item and the 2-units-above point item. Nothing asks the pupil to spot an incorrectly completed half or to work from a figure with several vertices at once.

competency_alignment.rationale: Difficulty moves from a plain point, to a polygon vertex, to a wing with multiple matching dots, which is a coherent build toward completing a whole symmetric figure rather than an unrelated escalation.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: No ceiling is stated by this competency, and the distances chosen keep every reflection inside a small grid, with the doubled-distance trap of 6 units against the correct 3 included as a distractor for the common misconception.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Both halves of the competency are exercised, pictorial models and numerals, in both directions. The flaw is one option set: the blocks item with key 7554 offers 21 alongside 7544 and 7454, and a two-digit value cannot arise from any reading of a four-digit block picture, so that option is dead weight a pupil discards immediately.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Two genuinely different pictorial models are used, base-10 blocks and the number line, and each is presented in both directions, once asking the pupil to build the representation for a given numeral and once asking for the numeral shown by the representation.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Numerals are four digits throughout, which is what Grade 3 Quarter 1 establishes, and the instructions are single imperatives such as moving a dot to show a value on the number line, with no multi-clause reasoning.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Two interaction types appear, a constructed representation and a read-and-choose, and they are crossed against the two model types, so the four combinations of model and direction are all represented in eight samples.

competency_alignment.rationale: The near-miss options in the number line items, 9520 through 9523 around the key, force attention to the ones digit on a scaled line, which is exactly the representational precision this competency is about rather than an arithmetic skill.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Values run from 1410 to 9630, all strictly below the stated ceiling of 10 000 and all four-digit, so the representations stretch to the top of the range the competency names without crossing it.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Reading and writing are both covered, but the true/false branch is degenerate: all three such items, the 1410 claim, the nine thousand six hundred thirty claim and the six thousand seven hundred ninety-five claim, have key False. A pupil who answers False reflexively scores every one of them without reading the number words.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Numeral to word and word to numeral both occur several times, and the word forms exercise the awkward parts of the naming system, including the hyphenated tens such as eighty-eight and fifty-four and a value ending in a zero ones digit.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Every number is four digits with no zero-place complications beyond a trailing zero, and the word forms follow a single consistent pattern of thousands, hundreds and a hyphenated remainder, which is the Grade 3 Quarter 1 expectation.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Three response types appear and the direction of translation alternates, so the node offers production of the word form, production of the numeral, and verification of a claimed equivalence rather than a single translation drill.

competency_alignment.rationale: Distractor quality is uneven in a way that undercuts the progression. Some options are well chosen digit reversals such as four thousand five hundred fifty-seven against the key seven thousand five hundred fifty-four, but the false claim that 1410 is 'one hundred forty-one' names a three-digit number for a four-digit numeral, which any pupil rejects on length alone.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: All numerals fall between 1410 and 9630, inside the competency's 10 000 ceiling and high enough to require the thousands word, so the range matches the stated bound rather than lingering in easier three-digit territory.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Ordinal naming and ordinal symbols are both produced and positions of objects are described, with pupils and baskets standing in a row. One item is flawed, though: asking who arrived earlier between 100th place and 94th place offers 77th, 33rd, 21st and 94th, so only one of the two positions in the stem is available and the ordering judgement can be skipped.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The generator reaches the stated ceiling with the one hundredth item and covers the irregular ordinal forms, including 21st and 90th written as ninetieth, as well as the successor case that crosses from 99th to 100th, which is where the naming pattern is most likely to break down.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Contexts are concrete lines of pupils and baskets, the sentences are two short clauses, and the vocabulary stays within counting and ordering words, with no computation demanded beyond finding the next position.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Four distinct item shapes occur: word form for a given ordinal, symbol form for a spoken ordinal, the position that comes after a given one, and a situated description of someone's place in a row. Both cloze and mcq are used.

competency_alignment.rationale: Difficulty rises by moving from low, regular ordinals such as the sixth position toward high and irregular ones near 100th, which is the dimension this competency names; nothing substitutes arithmetic or place-value work for ordinal reasoning.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Ordinals range from 6th to 100th, ending exactly at the ceiling the competency states and including values in every decade band, so the upper bound is tested rather than approached.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The competency separates the place value of a digit from the value of a digit, and the generator conflates them. Asking for the place value of the digit 5 in 5210 is keyed 5000, while a separate item type asks what place the digit 5 is in within 3250 and answers tens. The same phrase is therefore taught with two different meanings inside one node.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: All three tasks the competency lists are generated: the place or place value of a digit, the value of a digit as in the claim about the digit 5 in the ones place of 9105, and recovering the digit from a stated place as in asking which digit is in the tens place of 8735.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Every numeral is four digits, matching the competency's stated scope, the place names used are only ones, tens, hundreds and thousands, and no item requires more than locating a digit or naming its value.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Three response types appear and the true/false items carry both keys, True for the 3250 tens claim and False for the 7639 hundreds claim, so the verification branch is not answerable by a fixed response as it is elsewhere in this packet.

competency_alignment.rationale: Several option sets include values built by prefixing a 1 to the digit, 15 in the 5210 item, 14 in the 4120 item, 13 in the 2360 item and a claimed value of 19 for the digit 9 in the thousands place. These correspond to no place-value misconception, unlike the genuinely diagnostic 50 and 5 options that sit beside them.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The competency specifies a 4-digit number and every sampled numeral, from 1305 to 9501, is exactly four digits, so the range neither falls short into three-digit work nor overreaches toward five-digit place values.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The rounding instruction is stated plainly and the keys are right, but the option sets undercut the task: when the target is the nearest 100 the choices offered are 200 / 210 / 0 / 201, so only one value is even a multiple of a hundred. A pupil who knows nothing except that a rounded answer ends in zeros can pick correctly without rounding anything.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: All three targets named in the wording are exercised on numbers of the right size: nearest 10 on 38 and 158, nearest 100 on 230 and on the four-digit 8438, nearest 1000 on 6952 and 6148. The half-way behaviour also shows up, since 'Round 700 to the nearest 1000.' is keyed 1000.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Stems are one short imperative sentence; the number-line framing adds a single lead clause before the same instruction. Nothing here demands reading stamina or vocabulary past early Grade 3.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Three presentations show up for a procedural skill: a bare fill-in, a four-option choice, and a version anchored to a marked point on a number line. That is a reasonable spread for a rounding objective, which does not naturally carry a story context.

competency_alignment.rationale: What moves from sample to sample is mostly the magnitude of the number, not the rounding decision itself. Cases sitting exactly on the five boundary (such as the 105 and 225 items) are mixed in without being distinguished from easy ones, so the ladder does not separate the hard judgment from the easy one.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Values run from two digits (83) to four digits (8438), which is the span a Grade 3 rounding objective covering tens through thousands needs. Nothing spills past the ten-thousand band this grade works in.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Here the symbols are named by the competency itself and the keys are exactly those symbols, chosen at seeds 44, 46, 502 and 601 or embedded in a full statement at seeds 43, 45 and 603. Every pair falls under the stated bound.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Both inequality directions are keyed, at seed 43 one way and seeds 45 and 603 the other; equality appears at seeds 502 and 601; and pairs of unequal digit length are tested at seeds 44 and 602, which is a distinct sub-skill from comparing two four digit numerals.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The reasoning is honest place value work, sharpest at seed 604 where only the tens digit distinguishes 3724 from 3744. Sentences stay to one or two clauses. Seed 605 is the one over-built stem, nesting a stated sign inside a truth judgement, but a Grade 3 reader can carry that.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: One of the three formats is non-functional. Seeds 42, 500, 501, 600, 602 and 605 are the entire true or false population and every one of them is keyed False, which means the format rewards a fixed response instead of a comparison and contributes no discriminating information at all.

competency_alignment.rationale: The axis that moves is how close the two numerals sit, running from thousands apart at seed 44 through hundreds at seed 600 down to twenty apart at seed 604 and identical at seed 502. Tightening that gap is precisely what makes this competency harder.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The stated ceiling is never approached: the largest numeral in the whole sample is 9877 at seed 45, and nothing at or near ten thousand appears. At the other end only three values below 1000 occur, namely 154, 300 and 624, so the span is tested almost entirely in its middle band.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Ordering is what is asked and ordering is what the keys record, as full arrangements rather than single picks. Both directions the wording demands are genuinely keyed, smallest-first and largest-first alike.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The 'and vice versa' half is not an afterthought here: descending arrangements appear in both the plain and the story shells, and set sizes run from three items up to six, so the work scales rather than staying at one length.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The story stems, such as the one about seashells collected by 5 friends, stay to one sentence of setup plus one instruction. Comparing five four-digit numerals is demanding but is precisely the demand this quarter intends.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Two shells are present and each carries both directions: a bare list of numerals to arrange, and a counting context where friends' totals are ordered. Neither shell monopolises the ascending or the descending case.

competency_alignment.rationale: Difficulty is tuned on the axis that belongs to ordering, namely how close the values are: clusters such as 9409, 9404, 9410, 9394, 9401 force a digit-by-digit read, while wider spreads like 671, 9995, 10000 can be settled by length.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The stated ceiling is actually reached, since 10000 itself appears in three of the sets, and smaller sets in the hundreds give the low end of the range without leaving it.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Reading and writing pesos does happen in both directions, words to symbol and symbol to words. But the clause about the centavo sign is never the thing being produced; forms like 9216¢ appear only as wrong options, so the sign is something pupils learn to reject rather than to write.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Of the three notations the wording names, only two are ever a keyed answer. The currency code appears in exactly one sample, 'How is ₱1325 written using the currency code PhP?', and the centavo sign in none; the two centavo items instead ask for a peso decimal, which is a different notation from the one the competency lists.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Writing four-digit amounts in words with hyphenated compounds like forty-eight is standard Grade 3 work, and the decimal-of-a-peso idea is introduced through money rather than through abstract decimal place value.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Every single stem opens with the same transcription request about how an amount is written, and no sample places money in a buying, paying or change-giving situation. Twelve renderings, one sentence frame.

competency_alignment.rationale: The axis that changes across samples is the translation direction and the size of the amount, both of which belong to this reading-and-writing objective rather than to computation.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Amounts run from ₱248 up to ₱9216, staying under the stated ₱10 000 limit while still reaching four digits, and the sub-peso end is represented by 25 and 50 centavos.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: All fourteen renderings are the identical multiple-choice frame beginning with the same three-word instruction; no truth judgment, no blank to fill, no error check, no context. competency_alignment.rationale: The distractors are always the key plus or minus one or two, as in the choices 9401 / 9399 / 9400 / 9402. variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Four shells carry the stories: open answer, four-option choice, a stated answer to accept or reject, and a check on another child's solution, and the truth judgments are genuinely mixed between True and False keys.

competency_alignment.rationale: Progression runs on addend size and on whether the situation is money or count, both of which are the competency's own dimensions, and the harder samples are the ones approaching four digits in both addends.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The ₱3321 plus ₱6679 item lands on exactly 10 000, the stated limit, and nothing crosses it, while three-digit money amounts give the lower end.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The clause about regrouping is honoured on both sides: 8413 minus 4110 needs no exchange in any column, whereas 9120 minus 1093 and 5609 minus 1839 both do, and one comparison situation asks how many more rather than how many are left.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The backward number-line stems instruct counting back by ones over enormous distances; one has the dot at 6398 moving backward 3715 numbers with the direction to just count back that many. variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Bare differences, total-and-one-part statements, backward jumps, classmate error checks and a how-many-more comparison all appear, and the truth judgments split between a True and a False key rather than leaning one way.

competency_alignment.rationale: Difficulty tracks the borrowing demand and the width of the two numbers, which is the axis that belongs to this subtraction objective.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Most values sit properly in the thousands, but one sample asks the difference between 18 and 10 water bowls and another works from 152. comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Only seed 43 rounds anywhere other than the thousands place. No sampled item estimates a four digit pair to the nearest ten or to the nearest hundred, so the whole competency has been narrowed to a single rounding rule applied mechanically, and the sub-cases a pupil most needs are absent.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Vocabulary and sentence length suit Grade 3, but the demand sits below grade because no estimating is needed to answer. variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Not one of the fifteen samples places the task in a context; every stem is a bare pair of numerals or a restatement of one. competency_alignment.rationale: What varies between seeds 43, 501 and 500 is the magnitude of the numerals, not the estimating judgement, and the distractor construction visible at seeds 501, 600 and 603 keeps the key as the only round value throughout. scale_appropriateness.rationale: Values do stay inside four digits, from 90 at seed 604 up to 9413 at seed 500. competency_fulfillment.rationale: Chains of three and four two-digit terms are evaluated and every total I verified is correct, including the four-term string 96 + 84 + 5 - 80 keyed 105. The operands respect the two-digit limit even where running totals pass one hundred.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Three-term and four-term chains both occur, addition-only chains sit alongside mixed ones, and subtraction appears in opening, middle and closing positions rather than always at the end.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Holding a running total across four two-digit steps with intermediate values under about two hundred matches this quarter, and the stems carry no reading burden beyond the expression itself.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Thirteen of the fourteen samples are naked expressions ending in a blank; only the marbles sample about Fidel wraps the chain in any situation. For a node about performing chained operations that is defensible, but the presentation is nearly monolithic.

competency_alignment.rationale: The clause about observing correct order of operations is never made the object of a question. scale_appropriateness.rationale: Every term stays at or under two digits as the wording requires, with the largest single operand in the nineties, and totals stop near two hundred.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Each item resolves into a chain of three or four two-digit amounts combining addition and subtraction, and the money strand named in the wording is carried by peso amounts throughout roughly two thirds of the set.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Both term counts the wording allows are generated, receiving and giving away are mixed in varying order, and non-money contexts with eggs, notebooks and mangoes sit beside the peso ones.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Agreement errors intrude, with one stem reading 'Then Dina receives 1 mangoes.' before asking for the total. Amounts as small as 3, 6, 8 and 1 also drop the arithmetic below what a Grade 3 second-quarter pupil should be stretched by.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Every one of the fourteen samples is the same running-transaction script: a person starts with an amount, then receives or gives away twice or three times, then is asked what they have now. Nothing is combined, compared, or worked backwards from; only the names, nouns and numbers rotate.

competency_alignment.rationale: What is varied across samples is the number of transactions and the mix of gains and losses, which is exactly the axis this three-to-four-number problem-solving objective rests on.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Individual amounts stay within two digits as stated, with the largest around ninety-eight, and totals remain under two hundred.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Products are asked for directly and each of the four tables named supplies a factor somewhere, with six, seven, eight and nine all appearing. The array and shading items tie the product to an area model rather than to recall alone.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Facts are drawn across the range of each table rather than clustering at the doubles, and both orders of a fact appear, since a nine times eight item sits alongside an eight times nine one.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Single-digit multiplication with an array to fall back on is the right demand for this quarter, and the equal-groups sentence about bowls in bags is one clause of setup plus one question.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Recall, arrays to count, a rectangle to shade, an equal-groups story, a truth judgment and a classmate's error to check all appear, and the error checks are keyed both ways rather than always accepting the work.

competency_alignment.rationale: Two different seeds return the identical item 'Shade all the squares inside the 4×9 rectangle.' with the same key, so seed variation is not always producing a new problem. The set also opens on '1 × 6 = 7. True or False?', a fact that belongs to the identity property rather than to table fluency.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Factors stay inside the tables named and products top out at sixty-four and seventy-two, which is exactly the band this objective occupies.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The applying half of the objective is well served, but the illustrating half is missing entirely. Nothing in the set shows a property through an array, a grouping picture or any model; even the distributive item 'Is 8 × (7 + 2) the same as (8 × 7) + (8 × 2)?' is settled by computing both sides rather than by seeing why they agree.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: All five clauses the wording enumerates do get generated: multiplying by one, multiplying by zero, reordering two factors, regrouping three factors, and distributing over a sum. The zero clause rests on a single sample, which is thin, but it is present.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Parenthesised expressions are used here because the competency itself describes grouping and distribution, so the notation is earned rather than imported, and the yes-or-no decision keeps the response demand light.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Ten of the sixteen samples are the same are-these-the-same comparison of two expressions. Only a couple ask for a product outright, and no property is ever named, described, or demonstrated by the pupil.

competency_alignment.rationale: The filler option 'Only when both are 0' appears in every choice list without ever being right, reducing a four-way decision to a coin flip between True and False. One item also pairs a genuine regrouping with a quietly altered factor, which risks teaching doubt about associativity rather than confidence in it.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Factors stay single-digit and the intermediate sums inside the distributive items stay small, so the arithmetic never distracts from the property being examined.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The two multiplier shapes the wording distinguishes are both computed: ordinary single-digit multipliers as in 69 times 3, and multipliers whose only non-zero digit leads, as in 'What is 108 × 80?' and the 43 times 200 item.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Two-digit and three-digit multiplicands with single-digit multipliers are well represented and regrouping appears both ways, but the four-digit sub-case is carried by one computation only, 1000 × 10, which is repeated across three separate seeds. One arithmetic instance is not coverage of a clause.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Multiplying by a multiple of ten by appending zeros to a simpler product is the intended third-quarter method, and nothing here requires a two-digit by two-digit algorithm the grade has not met.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Four question shells appear, yet every one of them presents a bare product; there is no equal-groups picture, no array, and no situation in which a multiplication of this size would arise.

competency_alignment.rationale: Because the same 1000 by 10 computation recurs three times, a quarter of the set contributes no new demand, and the difficulty otherwise moves only by digit count rather than by whether regrouping is needed.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The largest product is exactly 10 000, the stated ceiling, and it is reached rather than avoided, with 9900 and 8640 filling the band just below it.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The method the wording prescribes is the method the keys use: each factor is taken to a multiple of ten before multiplying, so 'Estimate the product: 43 × 32' resolves to 1200 and the 28 by 27 item to 900. The stems name estimation rather than exact computation.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Two-digit by two-digit and three-digit by two-digit pairings are both plentiful, but the wording also admits a one-digit second factor and no sample uses one; the smallest multiplier anywhere in the set has two digits.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Rounding two factors and multiplying tens by tens is the expected third-quarter step, and the resulting products stay in a range Grade 3 can reason about.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Four presentations carry the work rather than one: an open approximation, a choice, a statement to accept or reject, and a classmate's approximation to check. The truth judgments are keyed both True and False.

competency_alignment.rationale: The choice items surround the key with values one or two away, such as the set 1199 / 1201 / 1200 / 1202, so the only tidy number is always correct. The progression therefore varies factor size while leaving the actual decision trivial.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Estimated products run from 900 up to 10000, matching a two-to-three-digit by one-to-two-digit objective, and the 503 by 20 sample sits right at the top of that band.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Problems are posed in words and solved by multiplying, and the money clause is genuinely served by cost-per-item situations. The two-step cases chain correctly, as with the six packs of six markers at fifteen pesos keyed 540.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Both step counts the wording permits are produced: single multiplications for items in bags, and genuine two-step chains where shelves hold boxes which hold objects, or boxes hold packs which carry a price.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The two-step stems keep to two short sentences before the question, and the nesting of shelves, boxes and contents is concrete enough for a third-quarter Grade 3 reader to picture.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Equal groups, unit-price purchases and rectangular shelf arrangements all appear, and they are posed as open questions, choices, claims to judge, and another child's work to check.

competency_alignment.rationale: A few samples collapse the multiplication they are meant to practise. Where 'Coach Roel wants to buy 75 score cards that cost ₱1 each.' the answer is the quantity itself, and the six sets at three pesos item is a table fact dressed as a problem, so those rungs do not advance the one-to-two-step demand.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Products run from eighteen up to seven hundred and twenty, and the two-step results such as 180 stay inside the range this quarter's multiplication supports.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Each sample presents a sequence built from a repeating group that shifts by a fixed amount and asks which term is missing, which is the verb and the object the wording names. The keys are consistent with the structure, as with the run 43, 47, 41, 63, 67, ___, 83, 87 keyed 61.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Increasing and decreasing components are both produced, which is the main split. But the wording says missing term or terms, and every sample blanks exactly one position; the harder multi-blank case that the plural admits is never generated.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Groups of two or three terms shifting by ten, twenty, fifty or a hundred is a load a third-quarter Grade 3 pupil can hold, and the sequences are short enough to scan in one line.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Three of the eight samples print the stem 'What is the missing term (position 8) in the pattern?' with no terms shown at all, so as rendered they cannot be attempted; the remaining five are inline lists. No sample sets the pattern in any real context such as beads, tiles or days.

competency_alignment.rationale: The things that change between samples are the group length, the size and sign of the shift, and where the blank falls, all of which are properties of the pattern itself rather than of some unrelated dressing.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Terms stay in the tens through low hundreds, with the largest sequences beginning around 224, which keeps the pattern reasoning rather than the arithmetic as the difficulty.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The objective asks a pupil to explain how a pattern is generated, but each stem hands them the explanation first, stating that each group of numbers repeats and then the next group changes by the same amount, and asks only for the number involved. The generating rule is given away in the question, so nothing in the set requires the pupil to articulate anything.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Both the increasing and the decreasing direction are generated, with shifts of ten, twenty and fifty upward and of ten, fifty and a hundred downward, and group lengths of two and three both occur.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Three of the eight samples key a negative number, including -10 and -100, as the answer. Signed numbers are not part of Grade 3 work, and the stem itself offers the grade-appropriate alternative by asking what is added or subtracted, so accepting only a negative numeral demands notation the pupil has not met.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: All eight renderings share one sentence frame word for word, differing only in the sequence printed and in whether the response is typed or chosen. There is no second way of asking, no continuation task, and no request to produce a further term.

competency_alignment.rationale: Every option list carries 0, which cannot be the shift in a sequence that visibly changes, alongside arbitrary values such as -588 that correspond to nothing a pupil would compute. The only real variation between samples is the magnitude of the shift.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Sequence terms sit between the tens and the low hundreds, small enough that finding the difference between successive groups is the work rather than the subtraction itself.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Both representations the wording names are built out: equal jumps back along a number line to reach zero, and division recovered from a known product, as in the items that begin from a multiplication fact and ask for the related quotient.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The jump form appears with the count of jumps unknown and with the jump size given, and the inverse form appears in both directions, sometimes dividing by the first factor and sometimes by the second, so neither sub-case is a token.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Starting values stay at or below seventy-two and jump sizes are single digits, so the number line can actually be imagined, which is what an illustrating objective needs at this grade.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The number line exists only as a sentence to picture; nothing in the set presents an actual model, an array, or a grouping the pupil manipulates, which sits awkwardly under a competency whose first verb is to illustrate. Two seeds also return the same item 'Since 4 × 7 = 28, then 28 ÷ 4 = ___' with only the classmate's name changed.

competency_alignment.rationale: Divisors range from two through nine and the samples alternate between recovering a quotient and checking a claimed number of jumps, so the difficulty moves along this objective's own axis.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Dividends stay within the multiplication facts of this grade, from twelve up to seventy-two, which is the right band for a first encounter with division.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Every quotient asked for comes from a fact in the tables the wording names, with six, seven, eight and nine each appearing as the divisor, and the dividends are genuine products from those tables rather than arbitrary numbers.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: All four divisors are exercised and across a spread of the table, from the low end at fourteen divided by seven up to eighty-one divided by nine, so no table is represented by a single easy fact.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Quotients are single digits, the array items give a concrete fallback, and the sharing sentence about bowls among friends stays to one clause of setup, all matching a fourth-quarter Grade 3 pupil.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The set moves between a rectangular array described as 48 squares split into 6 equal rows, a shading task, bare number sentences, a sharing story, truth judgments and checks on another child's work. The error checks are keyed both ways, including one where the classmate is wrong.

competency_alignment.rationale: Harder and easier samples differ by which table fact is required and whether a model is supplied, both of which build division fluency rather than varying some incidental feature.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Dividends run from fourteen to eighty-one, exactly the range spanned by the six, seven, eight and nine tables, with nothing reaching beyond them.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: One sample keys a true statement as false: '72 ÷ 8 = 9. True or False?' is answered False, while another sample in this same node, 'What number goes in the blank: 72 ÷ 8 = ___?', is keyed 9. The node contradicts itself on identical arithmetic, and a pupil answering correctly would be marked wrong.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The unknown is placed in several positions rather than one: in the dividend, in the quotient, and in the factor slot of a multiplication, and both operations the wording allows are represented.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The balance framing and the plain prose version asking what divided by eight equals five both stay short, and all the facts involved are single-digit results within this grade's tables.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: A balance model, a symbolic blank, a prose question, a claim about a missing number to judge, and another child's answer to check all appear, so the same missing-number idea is met from several angles.

competency_alignment.rationale: Two samples step outside the tables the competency names, one built on 2 × ? = 12 and one on '27 ÷ 4 = 3. True or False?', which is not even a whole-number division. Those items exercise something other than the six, seven, eight and nine facts this node is for.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Values stay within table products, reaching eighty-one at the top, so the numbers themselves are pitched correctly for this quarter.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: All three divisor families the wording sets out are actually divided: single-digit divisors on two and three-digit dividends, a remainder case, and division by ten, by one hundred and by one thousand, each of which appears with a correct key.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The with-remainder clause is the thinnest by far. Only one sample keys a remainder answer, 8 R 4, with one further statement to judge in the form '51 ÷ 8 = 7 R 3. True or False?'; the other twelve divide exactly, so a clause given equal weight in the wording gets a twelfth of the output.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Dividing by powers of ten by dropping zeros, and short division such as 158 by 2, are both fourth-quarter methods, and the remainder notation is introduced consistently in the items that use it.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Open blanks, choices, statements to verify and classmate checks all appear, and the choice list for the remainder item offers rival remainders rather than unrelated numbers, which is the right way to present that case.

competency_alignment.rationale: The samples move between structurally different divisions, place-value shifts on one hand and genuine short division on the other, which is precisely the contrast this competency is built from.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Dividends span two digits up to the four-digit 6920 and 6540, matching the two-to-four-digit range stated, and quotients stay comfortably within Grade 3.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Most items round both numbers to convenient multiples before dividing, which is the stated method. But one sample certifies a classmate's approximation of 15 for 34 divided by 2, a division whose exact answer is 17 and which a Grade 3 pupil can simply perform. Endorsing an estimate that is worse than the easy exact answer misrepresents when estimation is useful.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Both divisor widths the wording allows appear, single-digit divisors in the items dividing by 5 and by 2 and two-digit divisors throughout the rest, and the dividend is rounded sometimes to a multiple of ten and sometimes to a multiple of a hundred, as the wording provides for.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: After rounding, each item reduces to a single-digit or small quotient that follows from a known fact, so the reasoning stays within a fourth-quarter pupil's reach.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Four shells carry the work and the truth judgments split between a True and a False key, so no single response pattern succeeds across the set.

competency_alignment.rationale: Unlike the other estimation nodes, the choice lists here include an order-of-magnitude trap such as 50 sitting beside a key of 5, which targets the place-value slip this competency exists to prevent rather than merely testing tidiness.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Dividends range from the mid two digits to 807 and divisors from 2 to 87, which keeps every sample inside the two-to-three-digit by one-to-two-digit band stated.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The problems and their arithmetic are sound, but the money items answer in bare numbers while the stems use the peso sign; the one where Nikka has ₱42 to share between 2 friends is keyed 21 with options carrying no currency mark. For a competency that explicitly takes in money, an amount stripped of its unit is a half answer.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Both meanings of division are produced rather than one: sharing a quantity equally among a number of friends, and finding how many containers are needed when each holds a fixed amount. Money and object contexts both appear on each meaning.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Each stem is a single situation followed by a single question, and dividends such as 936 with a single-digit divisor keep the computation to the short division this quarter has established.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Open responses, choices, a claimed answer to accept or reject, and another child's solution to check all appear, and the truth judgments are keyed both ways rather than leaning one direction.

competency_alignment.rationale: Distractors are built from the errors this competency guards against, offering the divisor itself or the result of subtracting instead of dividing, so choosing correctly requires recognising that division is the operation.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Dividends run from two digits up to 936 with single-digit divisors throughout, matching the stated two-to-three-digit by one-digit range, and all divisions come out whole as that scope implies.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The descriptions are impossible as models. A stem stating that a shape is divided into 3 equal parts with 5 parts shaded asks a pupil to picture more shaded parts than the shape contains; a fraction greater than one needs more than one whole, and none of these items ever supplies a second shape. The wording of the competency is about representing such fractions with models, and no coherent model is described here.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Both cases the wording distinguishes are generated and keyed, fractions equal to one such as the eight-eighths and six-sixths items, and fractions greater than one across a range of denominators from halves to eighths.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Beyond the impossibility, some samples push past two whole units, as where a shape is divided into 8 equal parts and 18 parts are shaded. Holding more than two wholes in an unillustrated description is heavier than a first encounter with improper fractions should be.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Only two phrasings occur, one stating the shading inside the sentence and one splitting it into a second sentence, and neither is accompanied by a drawn region or a sharing situation such as pizzas or cakes that would make a fraction above one meaningful.

competency_alignment.rationale: What varies across samples is the denominator and how far the numerator exceeds it, including the exactly-equal case, which is the right dimension for an objective about fractions at and above one.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Denominators stay between two and eight, which is the range of unit fractions a Grade 3 pupil has met, and no sample asks for simplification or conversion beyond naming the fraction.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Both verbs of the competency are exercised on like denominators: addition appears as \(\frac{3}{8} + \frac{1}{8}\) and subtraction as \(\frac{7}{8} - \frac{1}{8}\), and the model requirement is honoured by the framing "A shape is divided into 8 equal parts" together with the shading tasks. Keys match their stems wherever the stem is self-contained; the two items reading "What is the result of the fraction operation shown?" store a letter key and cannot be checked against a picture this packet does not include.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Denominators range over 4, 5, 6, 8 and 10, but in all twelve samples the second fraction is one single part. Every addition item is phrased "1 more part is shaded" or adds 1/4, 1/6, 1/8, 1/10; every subtraction item is "1 shaded part is taken away" or subtracts 1/5, 1/6, 1/8. Nothing like adding two parts to three, or removing two of five, ever surfaces, so the operand variety the competency's plain wording permits is collapsed to a unit second term.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Stems stay to one or two short clauses built from Grade 3 vocabulary: "equal parts", "shaded", "taken away", "in all". The reasoning demanded is a single count of parts over an unchanged denominator, with no simplifying, renaming or mixed-number step imposed on the student, which is the right load for a Quarter 4 introduction to similar fractions.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Four presentation formats do appear (cloze, set_click, mcq, read_mcq), and "Shade the shape to show the result of 2/4 + 1/4." is a genuinely different task from picking an option.
